title: AI Video Ads Generator: Publish Checklist | AIVideosUGC
description: Use this checklist before publishing AI product photos or video ads. Compare the item, verify claims and prices, review rights, and check each platform’s rules.
h1: AI Video Ads Generator: A Pre-Publish Checklist
eyebrow: Check Every File Before You Post
lead: An AI Video Ads Generator can make a product clip quickly. Before you publish a photo or video ad, compare the product, claims, rights, and labels with the real item.
summary: Build the ad, match it to the product you ship, type the price yourself, and mark the file the way each site asks.

paras: Check the product, video, price, image rights, and platform labels before posting. Keep the real item or source photo beside your screen.
sections.alt: Adult hands hold a plain black travel backpack beside a blank laptop and a blank phone.

paras: An AI Video Ads Generator makes a short ad from a product photo or listing. You still review every frame and claim before publishing.

A generated photo or video is a new picture made from your upload, not a copy of the source. A letter can change, a part can move, or a color can shift. Use the same check on a listing photo, a social post, and a paid ad.
sections.alt: Hands check the front pocket and zipper of plain black travel backpack.

sections.h2: How Do I Review a Finished Video Ad?
paras: Watch the file the way a shopper will, on a phone, with the sound and the captions on. Start from the first frame.
A TikTok ad and a Meta ad both need the product to match. Meta here means Facebook and Instagram. A tall file and a square file can still show the same product.

sections.h2: How Do I Check the Product in the Picture?
paras: Hold the real product, or your original photo, next to the screen and go through color, shape, logos, parts, and size.

Compare the color in daylight. Count the parts. Read every letter on a label. If a hand is in the picture, the product should look the right size next to it. Extra scenery is fine only when a shopper can tell it is not part of the order. Those scenes are made as [lifestyle product photos](page:lifestyle-photos).
sections.alt: Hands count pockets, buckles and straps on plain black travel backpack.

sections.h2: What Is on a Video Ad Checklist?
paras: Play the clip on your phone. Listen to the voice, and read the captions. Then watch the hands and the first frame.

The script should name the product you ship. Do not mention a feature that is not for sale. Clips often go wrong while the product moves. Count the fingers, and watch how they hold the item. If one short moment looks wrong, trim it. If the problem runs through the whole clip, make a new version. Run this check on a [product video](page:product-videos) before you post it.
sections.alt: Hands open the zipper and flap of plain black travel backpack.

sections.h2: How Do I Add the Price Before I Publish?
paras: Make the picture or the clip first. Then add the price, the date, the code, and the headline yourself.
Do not ask the tool to paint those words into the image or the clip. Letters it draws are often wrong. Captions can match the spoken line. You still type the price, the date, and the code yourself.
sections.alt: Plain black travel backpack centered on a white background.

sections.h2: What Do I Need to Own Before an Ad Goes Live?
paras: Upload only photos you took, or photos you have permission to use. Use only logos that belong to you.

If the photo comes from a supplier, your agreement must cover ads. A request built around another company's logo, or a celebrity, may be refused. The [Content Policy](/content) says what you can upload. For music, pick a track from the music library, or one you already licensed.
sections.alt: Hands hold plain black travel backpack beside a plain camera and blank phone.

paras: Read the current rule on each site you post to. Several sites ask you to mark a realistic generated face or scene. Check again before a big spend.
Do not show a generated face as a buyer or a reviewer. That includes [model photos for clothing](page:model-photos). Do not let a caption promise a health, skin, or weight result.
A script can start from your product page, but only you can confirm that its claims match the item you ship.

The file comes out in a shape you pick before the job. Those shapes are listed on [pricing](page:pricing). 9:16 is a tall phone video. 1:1 is a square. 16:9 is a wide video. 4:3 and 3:4 are there too.
From one photo you can ask for a calm try-on and a louder unboxing. Keep the version that fits the shop after you run the check.

sections.h2: How to Create a Video Ad in 3 Steps
paras: Add the product page. Or write a short note about what you are advertising. [URL to video](page:url-to-video) is there if you do not want to retype the name.
An adult face comes from the [actor library](page:ai-actors). The tool matches a presenter and a voice, then you review the clip before you trust it.
Download in the shape you need, or hand the file to the ad account. The download has no watermark.

sections.h2: What You Gain From an AI Video Ad
paras: You can trim the clip yourself, and you do not book a camera day just to test the ad.

You pay with credits on a monthly plan. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. A photo costs 24 credits, and each video charge appears before it starts.
When the first ad only shows the product closed, make another file that shows the detail that sells. Check that new file before you post it.
When a live ad starts to feel familiar, change the room and keep the product. Review the new file before it replaces the old one.
You pick the tone, the avatar, and the colors. You can edit the script before the voice is set.
Use the avatar, the voice, and a song from the music library on ads you download here. Or bring a song you already licensed for ads.

sections.h2: More Video Tools for the Same Photo
paras: Turn the product photo into a [product video](page:product-videos). Or start from the [video tools](page:video-hub) if you are still choosing a format.
A clip of an avatar talking about the product is on [UGC video ads](page:video-ads). A post for the feed can follow [Instagram ads](page:plat-instagram).
Paste the listing if you do not want to type the details again. That tool is [URL to video](page:url-to-video).
Pick a face in the [actor library](page:ai-actors), or save one look and use it on the next product.
If the photo should simply start to move, use [image to video](page:image-to-video). Then run this check on the clip.
A large catalog can send each product through and get a file back. You see the credit cost before each one starts.

sections.h2: AI Video Ads vs Filming the Ad
paras: Timing. You upload a photo or paste a listing, then review a clip. You do not book a day with a crew.
Cost. You spend credits from the monthly plan. A filmed ad also pays the people and the place.
Versions. A second opening is a new file from the same photo, not another day of filming.
Control. You can change a word before anyone hears it. On a hired shoot, that change often waits until the day.
Rights. You start from photos you are allowed to use, and a song from the library or one you already licensed. A creator's face and music often need a separate agreement.
Next product. The next item uses the same steps. You do not wait on one person's calendar.

sections.h2: How Shops Use a Checked Video Ad
paras: A bag seller shows an AI avatar holding the product and naming one part. A person checks that part against the real item before anyone posts it.
A gadget seller opens the box on a desk and confirms every part in the kit is the part that ships.
A clothing seller shows the piece on an adult, then matches the neckline and the print to the sample before the file is saved.
A food seller sets the jar on a counter. The voice names the flavor printed on the lid, and no extra claim is added after the check.
Match the photo or clip to the product you ship. Verify the price and claims, confirm your rights, then follow each platform’s labeling rules.
Send it to TikTok or Meta, or download it, only after those checks. If a shopper could feel misled, do not post that file.

faq.q: Can I create ads for many products?
faq.a: Yes. Make a separate ad for each product and review each result. This saves filming time when you have a large catalog.

faq.q: Can I use a supplier photo as the source?
faq.a: Only if your agreement with the supplier covers ads. Otherwise shoot your own photo of the item.

faq.q: What should I check before posting an AI-made video?
faq.a: Check the product, voice, captions, and any price from start to finish. Watch the finished ad on your phone before posting.
Use AI ads for quick tests and large catalogs, and hire creators when a real person’s endorsement matters. Review every AI ad before publishing.

faq.q: How much does it cost to make a video for review?
faq.a: Starter costs $24.50 monthly for 200 credits, Pro $35 for 300, and Premium $63 for 600. Videos use 24 to 120 credits by length.

faq.q: How do I review an AI-generated product video?
faq.a: Watch the full video with sound before publishing. Check product details, spoken claims, captions, and any price against what customers will receive.

faq.q: Will TikTok or Meta block an AI ad?
faq.a: They may reject an AI ad if it breaks their current rules or makes a misleading claim. Check each platform’s policies before you pay to run it.

faq.q: Which sizes can I export, and where do they run?
faq.a: You can export 9:16 for TikTok and Stories, 1:1 for feeds, and 16:9 for wide placements. Check the ad preview before spending.

faq.q: What should I check before publishing an AI ad?
faq.a: Check that your product looks right, every claim is true, and the price matches your store. Review captions, usage rights, and platform labels before posting.

faq.q: What if one moment in the clip looks wrong?
faq.a: Make a new version if a mistake appears throughout the video. For one brief mistake, remove that moment and review the full video again.

faq.q: How do I add a discount code to an AI ad?
faq.a: Add the code in the editor after making the image so every character is correct. Check the price and end date before posting.

faq.q: Should I review a still product image too?
faq.a: Yes. Compare its color, shape, parts, labels, and scale with the item customers will receive.

faq.q: Can the file run as a paid ad?
faq.a: Yes. Commercial use is included on a paid plan, and the download has no watermark.

faq.q: What if an extra object looks like it comes with the order?
faq.a: Do not use that version, or say clearly in the listing what is included. Decoration is fine only when a shopper would not expect it in the box.
